sources.outlet: U.S. EPA Region 7, State Review Framework: Nebraska Clean Air Act Implementation in FFY2022 (Final Report)
sources.quote: NDEE did not conduct any formal enforcement responses during the review period and therefore no penalties were assessed, collected or documented in the data or files.
sources.searcher_note: EPA's own review, FFY2022 only: NDEE 'is not engaging in formal enforcement to address and resolve HPVs' per EPA policy. Same report also finds 2 of 9 HPVs 'still showing up in ICIS-AIR as active, even though they had been resolved and documented with NDEE's database' (backs the lead's caveat).

sources.outlet: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (DWEE), Enforcement Actions
sources.quote: Archer Daniels Midland Company FID 9169 Programs (AIR) Clean Air Act
sources.searcher_note: State's own enforcement list shows a Clean Air Act consent order, Case No 3650, dated 2025-10-22. The list (dwee.nebraska.gov/news-events/enforcement-actions) shows other state air-program orders in the window: Western Sugar 2017-19, Gothenburg Feed 2017, Greencycle 2018, AltEn 2018-22, Frenchman Valley 2019, Green Disposal Mead 2020, Vontz Paving 2020, Tecumseh Poultry 2023, POET Fairmont 2024. Disagrees with 'zero formal actions', unless those never reached EPA's air database.

sources.searcher_note: Second example of a state air-program consent order in the window: Case Number 3581, Consent Order dated 2022-02-16. The linked PDFs are scanned images with no text layer.

sources.outlet: NDEE Annual Report to the Legislature, 2022
sources.quote: The department has only needed to pursue formal enforcement 183 times since 2014; only 1 percent of all department inspections result in formal enforcement proceedings.
sources.searcher_note: Agency describes its low formal-enforcement rate as a goodwill approach. All programs combined, not air alone.

sources.outlet: Nebraska DWEE, Air Compliance & Enforcement Program page
sources.quote: Through the Nebraska Environmental Protection Act, the Air Program attempts to obtain compliance with environmental regulations first through voluntary efforts.
sources.searcher_note: Agency policy: voluntary compliance first; enforcement 'when compliance issues are serious, chronic, or cannot be otherwise resolved'; works through the Attorney General.

sources.outlet: U.S. EPA Region 7, Nebraska SRF Round 2 (Final Report January 4, 2012)
sources.quote: Lack of Administrative penalty authority delays bringing source back into compliance
sources.searcher_note: Earliest EPA finding on the same pattern for Nebraska's CAA program: low HPV discovery rate, HPVs entered late into AFS, no administrative penalty authority. Old window (pre-2017).

notes: No news story found reporting Nebraska's zero formal air actions in EPA's database 2017-2025, the 0 of 17 HPVs resolved, or the 15 of 120 majors 'Unaddressed'. The primary-record match is EPA's own SRF report (FFY2022): NDEE took no formal enforcement and isn't using formal enforcement to resolve HPVs. Disagreement: DWEE's own enforcement-actions list shows state Clean Air Act consent orders in most years 2017-2025 (e.g., ADM 2025, POET 2024, Tecumseh Poultry 2023, Green Plains 2022), and the SRF says some HPVs resolved in NDEE's database still show active in ICIS-Air, so the lead's zero count may be a data-entry gap. Seen, not recorded: Nebraska Examiner 2022-09-30 (NDEE says it relies on 'voluntary' compliance, CAFO/water context), AltEn coverage (Grist, Nebraska Public Media) on slow enforcement, mostly water and waste. The WebSearch tool appeared to run several sub-searches on query 5. No coverage dated July-Sept 2026 found.
